\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{పోటీ} (pōṭī)}{పోటీ (pōṭī)}]{\te{పోటీ} (pōṭī) — a competition, a match}

\label{lesson:TE-C189-poti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a bindi, then the Telugu for henna.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పోటీ}}
\textbf{\te{పోటీ}} — \emph{pōṭī} — \textquotedblleft{}a competition, a match\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{పోటీ}} (\emph{pōṭī}) is native Dravidian, one word with Tamil \emph{pōṭi} and Kannada \emph{pōṭi} (DEDR 4583). DEDR lists Telugu \emph{pōṭi}, \textquotedblleft{}competition, rivalry\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\te{అభిరుచి}} (\emph{abhiruci}) is Sanskrit \emph{abhiruci}, \textquotedblleft{}liking, delight\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama. It is built on \emph{ruci}, which CDIAL 10762 glosses \textquotedblleft{}light, beauty\textquotedblright{}.
